clinician.final_diagnosis: CNS PTLD, specifically high-grade diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) of the activated B-cell phenotype
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 64-year-old woman who underwent liver transplantation 18 months prior for autoimmune hepatitis, maintained on mycophenolate and tacrolimus immunosuppression, presented with acute neurological symptoms including generalized weakness, headaches, confusion, disorientation, and focal neurological deficits (left-sided hemiparesis, sensory changes, pyramidal signs, visuospatial deficits). Physical examination revealed papilledema indicating increased intracranial pressure. Initial brain CT without contrast ruled out hemorrhage. Brain MRI revealed multiple ring-enhancing lesions (largest 2.7 cm) in the right frontal, temporoparietal, and left parietal lobes with moderate vasogenic edema, consistent with intracranial lymphoma. Urgent brain biopsy was performed, which demonstrated diffuse infiltrates of intermediate to large mononuclear cells with CD20+ B-cell marker expression, confirming B-cell lymphoma. Serological testing ruled out common opportunistic infections (CMV, Toxoplasma, Hepatitis B/C, HIV). The patient was treated with systemic rituximab and methotrexate chemotherapy (8 cycles), resulting in clinical improvement. Follow-up brain MRI at 14 months post-treatment showed improved imaging findings, confirming treatment response. The clinical presentation, imaging characteristics, histopathology findings, immunophenotype (CD20+ B cells), immunosuppressed transplant status, and excellent response to rituximab-based chemotherapy are all consistent with CNS PTLD/DLBCL.
